newsitem.title: USA: Brent dips in late trade, US foreign crudes ample.
newsitem.headline: Brent dips in late trade, US foreign crudes ample.

text.p: North Sea Brent crude dropped in the U.S. aftermarket late Monday in a continuing downward trend blamed on a preponderance of sellers, traders said.
A series of partial paper April Brent cargoes changed hands at $21.96/21.97/22.00/22.01/22.02 a barrel, down from $22.17 a barrel in the IPE settlement, traders said.
"There's more selling interest than buying interest," said one Northeast broker.
February/March Brent spreads traded three times at 28 cents, while March/April traded once at 41 cents, steady with the London close.
Meanwhile, foreign crudes continue to stream into the U.S. Gulf Coast, putting renewed pressure on domestic grades and short-haul barrels from Latin America.
A Vasconia cargo from Colombia is still looking for a home for the end of January and is now considered distressed, traders said.
Two companies are showing early March Brent cargoes at around March WTI minus 40-50 cents barrel, while another is trying a sell a VLCC loading at the end of January, traders said.
Traders also reported availabilities of spot Saudi and Kuwaiti barrels, as well as West African Forcados.
The onslaught of foreign cargoes amid a series of turnarounds and weak margins on the Gulf Coast has softened the fundamental picture considerably.
"By the end of the week, crude will be offered on the water," noted one trader.
